title: Why the Map Outgrows the Count

scenes.tts: The first film turned recombinant offspring into a short chromosome ruler. Why does that ruler fail when the interval grows? Reuse the blue and gold homologues. Move their outside markers apart, and let more crossover sparks fall between them. The map keeps growing, but the observed count cannot follow forever.
scenes.caption: The first film turned recombinant offspring into a short chromosome ruler. Why does that ruler fail when the interval grows? Reuse the blue and gold homologues. scenes.visual: Reuse film one's exact colour map: BLUE homologue with A—B, GOLD homologue with a—b. Stretch the outside markers apart. Crossover sparks accumulate while a chromosome ruler extends rightward. Beneath it, a recombinant gauge labelled 'schematic' rises but begins bending.
scenes.narration: The first film turned recombinant offspring into a short chromosome ruler. Why does that ruler fail when the interval grows? Reuse the blue and gold homologues. scenes.visual: Brief title over the carried chromosome pair: 'Why the Map Outgrows the Count'. Keep crossover sparks drifting through the widened interval.

scenes.tts: A two-point cross does not count crossover events. It reads only the final combination of the outside markers. One exchange between them flips a parental combination into a recombinant one. Another exchange can flip that combination again. The gamete remembers its ending, not the number of turns.

scenes.visual: Zoom to one BLUE and one GOLD chromatid. Put a large state badge below: 'parental'. Animate one reciprocal swap between outside markers and flip the badge to 'recombinant'. Leave room for another crossover spark without triggering it yet.
scenes.narration: A two-point cross does not count crossover events. It reads only the final combination of the outside markers. scenes.tts: The chromatid now looks recombinant at the outside markers. What will those markers show after another crossover lands inside the same interval? Follow only their colours, not the crossed segments in the middle.
scenes.caption: The chromatid now looks recombinant at the outside markers. What will those markers show after another crossover lands inside the same interval? Follow only their colours, not the crossed segments in the middle.
scenes.visual: Hold the mixed-colour chromatids with the state badge reading 'recombinant'. Pulse a second potential crossover site farther right. Put question marks beside only the two outside marker dots.
scenes.narration: The chromatid now looks recombinant at the outside markers. What will those markers show after another crossover lands inside the same interval? Follow only their colours, not the crossed segments in the middle.

scenes.visual: Keep both outside markers large. A thin tracing glow travels from left marker through the crossed middle toward the right marker, then stops before revealing the final state.

scenes.tts: The second flip can restore the parental outside combination. The middle still records exchanged material, but a two-point score misses it. Even numbers of effective flips look parental. Odd numbers look recombinant. Long intervals contain more hidden histories that finish with the same visible answer.

scenes.visual: Animate the second reciprocal swap. Flip the state badge back to 'parental' while preserving alternating BLUE and GOLD blocks in the middle. Split the frame into two moving lanes labelled 'even → parental' and 'odd → recombinant'.
scenes.narration: The second flip can restore the parental outside combination. The middle still records exchanged material, but a two-point score misses it. scenes.tts: Across many meioses, repeated flips make parental and recombinant endings equally likely. Recombination frequency therefore approaches its ceiling. So distant linked loci can look unlinked, like loci on different chromosomes. A two-point result at the ceiling cannot distinguish those cases.

scenes.visual: Feed many animated chromatid histories into two final-state bins labelled 'schematic'. The bins settle to equal heights. Put '50% ceiling' on screen only, never spoken. Beside them, show a distant linked pair and a pair on different chromosomes converging on the same display.

scenes.tts: Now plot what the count can see against map distance. Use Haldane's no-interference equation, not a sketch. The computed curve starts close to a straight line, then bends toward the ceiling. Distance continues across the axis while the observable frequency loses sensitivity.
scenes.caption: Now plot what the count can see against map distance. Use Haldane's no-interference equation, not a sketch. The computed curve starts close to a straight line, then bends toward the ceiling. Distance continues across the axis while the observable frequency loses sensitivity.
scenes.visual: Transform the equal bins into a full-frame computed curve from RF = (1 − exp(−2d)) / 2. Label axes 'map distance' and 'recombination frequency'. Mark the horizontal 50% ceiling on screen. A tracer moves right as its vertical gain shrinks.
scenes.narration: Now plot what the count can see against map distance. Use Haldane's no-interference equation, not a sketch. The computed curve starts close to a straight line, then bends toward the ceiling. Distance continues across the axis while the observable frequency loses sensitivity.

scenes.tts: A third marker breaks a long span into shorter intervals. Count each short interval where fewer exchanges stay hidden. Place those distances end to end on one chromosome. Their map distances add. Their raw recombination frequencies do not, because the whole-span count can erase double crossovers.

scenes.visual: Return to the BLUE and GOLD chromosomes. Drop a TEAL middle marker between the outside markers. Bracket the two short intervals, convert each to a map segment, and snap the segments end to end. Cross out two schematic RF gauges being added.

scenes.tts: The computed curve is a model, not a universal correction. Haldane assumes independent crossover placement. Interference changes how often nearby crossovers occur, so another function may fit better. The durable practice is to map short intervals, add their distances, and state the model behind any correction.

scenes.visual: Keep the computed Haldane curve labelled 'independent crossovers'. Add a second dashed curve labelled 'schematic interference model', with no claim of universality. Then return focus to the tiled short-interval chromosome map.

scenes.tts: The count reports a final marker state. The map represents the expected number of crossovers per chromatid across the interval. Those quantities track closely only while hidden exchanges are rare. As the interval grows, the map can keep lengthening after the count has nearly stopped changing.

scenes.visual: Place the final-state bins beside the extending genetic map. Freeze the bins near equal height while the map continues extending. Fade the bins and leave the long map with two hidden crossover sparks glowing.

scenes.visual: Show one centered line only: 'Over long intervals, hidden crossovers make recombination frequency underestimate distance.'
